solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Idiot — he is quiet, say, as one stuck on the line?

parts.note: a clot is a fool, a dimwit
contracted to he's, apostrophe dropped
p (piano) is the musical mark for quiet
e.g., for example, as 'say' introduces an instance

explanation.surface: Someone insults a quiet man as a useless hanger-on.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the thing 'stuck on the line' is pinned to a washing line.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden clip pinches wet laundry onto the washing line to dry, so it is literally stuck there.

clue.text: Revival of firm needing this person (sponsor)

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
the setter speaking of themself: me
to back someone is to support or fund them

explanation.surface: A business recovers thanks to the backing of a single sponsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A return to former success or popularity is a revival, as of a performer's career.

clue.text: Herb with old air-gun disturbed maidens

indicators.note: letters that are disturbed are thrown out of order, so the weapon's letters are mixed

parts.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for maiden overs

explanation.surface: An antique air rifle has upset some young women, oddly connected to a herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges AIRGUN into RIGANU. A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the botanical genus of marjoram and oregano, aromatic plants used in cooking.

clue.text: Some treachery undoes cabinet minister

indicators.note: to undo something is to take it apart, so the letters of the phrase are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A government minister is brought down by betrayal within.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is the senior minister in charge of policing, immigration and internal affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The holder of this office sits in the British Cabinet, running the Home Office.

clue.text: Out-of-control car alas crushes worker somewhere in California

indicators.note: the scrambled letters squeeze around the insect, holding it within
a vehicle out of control is all over the place, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A runaway car flattens a labourer at some Californian spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out-of-control' and 'crushes' read as a road accident; the ant is the standard crossword worker.
explanation.definitionFit: This city sits in Silicon Valley in the San Francisco Bay Area, a specific place in that state.

clue.text: Make incisions in wet chalk

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the phrase, spanning the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: Someone scratches marks into damp chalk.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave a design by cutting lines into a surface, often with acid, is to make incisions.

clue.text: Rake caught by rules and regulations

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the law is the body of rules a society enforces

explanation.surface: A libertine is finally brought to book by the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake' looks like the noun for a dissolute man, but it is the verb meaning scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: To rake with nails or talons is to scratch or tear at something, a verb sense.

clue.text: Deception despicable? Don't show your face!

parts.note: a lie is a deception, an untruth
a low trick is mean and contemptible

explanation.surface: After a shameful deceit, a culprit is told to hide away.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep out of sight and stay hidden is the idiom meaning don't show yourself.

clue.text: Insect that's small and nasty, lacking tail

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

indicators.note: the word for nasty loses its final letter, its tail

parts.note: vile means foul or nasty

explanation.surface: A tiny, unpleasant bug lacks a tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking tail' cuts the last letter from VILE, leaving VIL.
explanation.definitionFit: This beetle with a long snout is a crop and grain pest, an insect.

clue.text: Buddy in ship coming to Spanish waters?

indicators.note: the crewman arrives at the waters, so his letters follow theirs

parts.note: the Spanish Main was the Caribbean coast and sea once ruled by Spain
one in a ship is a man aboard, a hand of the crew

explanation.surface: A friend sails into the Caribbean on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a best friend or closest companion, a buddy.

clue.text: Take part in contest and finish 50 short

indicators.note: the word for finish falls short by losing the numeral

parts.note: to complete a task is to finish it
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An athlete enters a race and ends fifty metres behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes L from COMPLETE.
explanation.definitionFit: To vie against rivals is to compete, taking part in a contest.

clue.text: Mother turning up with one boy on a sports ground maybe somewhere in NY

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
I is the Roman numeral one
a son is a male child
a sports ground is one example of a venue

explanation.surface: A mother arrives with her lad at a sports ground in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses DAM to MAD. This New York street is famous as the home of the advertising industry.
explanation.definitionFit: This Manhattan avenue is a specific place in New York, so it fits a vague place-name definition.

clue.text: Senior officer needing support squatted, keeping quiet!

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: the past tense of sitting holds the hush word within it

parts.note: squatted means sat on one's haunches
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A top officer, wanting support, sat down and kept silent.
explanation.walkthrough: The support is an undergarment, not military backup.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a high-ranking military officer, from the gold braid on the cap.

clue.text: Skimpy item of clothing? Daughter has fashionable one

parts.note: hot means in vogue, trendy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A daughter owns a trendy, revealing outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: This loincloth worn by Hindu men in India is a garment that covers little.

clue.text: Condition of some women in emotional state about 'the right house'

indicators.note: the feeling word goes about, around, the other pieces

parts.note: a mood is a state of mind or feeling

explanation.surface: Some women grow emotional about finding the ideal home.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'the right house' look like a phrase, but each word gives its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a mother is the state that some women are in.

clue.text: Louche cousin messing about in rented accommodation

indicators.note: fooling around suggests disorder, so the letters of both words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A disreputable relative misbehaves in a rented flat.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is a home rented out cheaply by the local council, social housing.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a home is owned by local government and let to tenants, so it is rented accommodation.

clue.text: Little girl or boy may be upset, being undressed

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the string upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: Deb is a short form of Debbie or Deborah
taken as written
Sid is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A small child might be distressed at having clothes removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be upset' reverses DEBORSID as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stripped of one's robes or clothes is to be undressed.

clue.text: Letter acting again maybe as something that is liberating?

definitions.meaning: a landlord who lets a property again is a ..., a letter in the renting sense
a device or agent that sets something free

explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' is one who lets, not a character of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: One who frees or lets go of something performs liberation; hyphenated, one who leases again.

clue.text: Chinese anger about internet facility

indicators.note: all about, scattered around, so the letters of both words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Chinese fury is directed at an online service.
explanation.definitionFit: A website that finds pages by keyword, like Google, is an internet tool.

clue.text: Animals being shy with inadequate thrust

parts.note: coy means bashful

indicators.note: the word for thrust is not complete, falling short by its last letter

parts.note: a push is a shove or thrust

explanation.surface: Timid creatures make only a feeble push.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inadequate' cuts PUSH to PUS.
explanation.definitionFit: These large South American water rodents, also called nutria, are animals.

clue.text: A king's inscription at the foot of tablet forming a monument?

indicators.note: in a down clue the inscription sits below the tablet, so its letters come after

parts.note: a pill is a medicinal tablet
R for Rex is the royal letter inscribed on coins and ... boxes

explanation.surface: A king's words are carved at the base of a stone slab, making a memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tablet' suggests a stone slab but is a pill.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall column such as Nelson's is a monument, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Board expressing agreement bilingually

parts.note: yes in two languages: French oui and German ja
the second language's yes, German ja

explanation.surface: A committee says yes in two languages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' suggests a committee but is a spirit-message board.
explanation.definitionFit: This lettered board is used in seances to spell out messages from spirits.

clue.text: Noisy party-goers in the middle of hotels making one cross

indicators.note: the revellers sit in the core letters of the lodging word
only the central pair of letters of the word is taken

parts.note: ravers are revellers at loud dance parties

explanation.surface: Loud revellers in the hotels make one guest angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like the adjective for angry but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To go across a mountainside or region is to cross it, a verb sense.

clue.text: Prominent Indian has a pint rolling over

indicators.note: turning over end to end, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a pint of beer

explanation.surface: An important Indian man knocks over his beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling over' reverses AJAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian prince or king, a person of rank and prominence.

clue.text: Tree in China by army ground

parts.note: china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, a pal

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree in China stands beside soldiers on their parade ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' with its capital looks like the country, but china is rhyming slang for mate. 'ground' turns ARMY into MYRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall Asian fan palm, the toddy palm, is a tree.

clue.text: British honour given to writer (American) for collection of novels?

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
a nib is the writing tip of a pen
US for United States

explanation.surface: An American author receives a British honour for his novels.
explanation.definitionFit: A single volume collecting several works by one author is a compendium of novels.

clue.text: Kind to get drunk clutching end of bar

indicators.note: the drinker holds onto the final letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A kindly person gets drunk, hanging onto the end of the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like an adjective but is the noun for type.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety or type is a kind, as in 'that sort of thing'.

clue.text: Music supremo didn't allow German songs to be heard

indicators.note: spoken out, the phrase matches another word in sound

parts.note: banned (didn't allow) plus lieder (German art songs)

explanation.surface: A conductor prohibited German songs from performance.
explanation.definitionFit: The person directing a dance band or jazz orchestra is in charge of the music.
